subject: Invoice round-off & context apportionment for committed pack
messages:
From: Tim Lee <tim.lee@brightcart.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@brightcart.com, Maria Gonzalez <maria.g@brightcart.com>
Date: Fri, 14 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Question on April invoice rounding and context allocation

Jordan —

We received the April invoice and our accounting team flagged two items: the token rounding behavior and how long-context usage (we push many 16k prompts) was split across the committed pack. On the invoice line items it looks like some calls were billed as full 8k units even when only ~3.9k tokens were new; that doubled the per-call charge relative to our expectation.

We believe our contract (attached) said: 500k monthly committed tokens, 10% discount, and context-length tolerances where long contexts should be apportionable across the pack when >50% reused. Can you confirm the calculation used for April? Please include the usage export if possible.

Appreciate a quick turnaround — our FP&A needs the explanation before our month-end close.

Thanks,
Tim
VP Product, BrightCart

Attachment: brightcart_april_invoice.pdf

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Tim Lee <tim.lee@brightcart.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 14 Jun 2028 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Question on April invoice rounding and context allocation

Hi Tim —

Thanks for the note and the invoice. I'm pulling the usage export and the pricing schedule we used (sending both) and will outline the math. Short answer: billing uses our "quantum" unit of 512 tokens for long-context apportionment by default which can cause apparent rounding up on many small deltas; however, there are two configurable behaviors that can change the outcome (prefix reuse crediting and per-request fractional apportionment).

I've looped in Vanessa (pricing) and Kimberly (billing ops) — Vanessa, can you confirm whether the account is on the fractional-apportionment toggle we prototyped for enterprise pilots? If not, Kimberly and I will run a quick re-calc and propose either a one-time invoice adjustment or a credit.

Jordan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: usage-export-april.csv, redwood_pricing-schedule-v2.pdf

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tim Lee <tim.lee@brightcart.com>, procurement@brightcart.com
Date: Mon, 17 Jun 2028 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Question on April invoice rounding and context allocation

Thanks Jordan / Tim —

Checked the account flags: BrightCart is NOT on the fractional-apportionment toggle. That means we apply token quantum rounding at invoice time per-call, and we also apply the committed-pack apportionment after grouping by model+region. For calls with heavy KV reuse we do prefix-crediting but only when reuse meets the stored-kv threshold (>=60% overlap) — the contract language you referenced used 50% so I see the mismatch. That's on us to reconcile.

Quick options:
- Short term (fast): run an ad-hoc re-billing for April using 50% overlap and fractional apportionment; offer a 1.5% one-time invoice credit to account for friction.
- Medium term (systemic): flip BrightCart to fractional-apportionment toggle for future invoicing and re-run May/June projections to validate savings.

Kimberly — can you produce the April line-level re-calc with the 50% overlap and fractional apportionment? Tim, if you want a sample subset earlier today I can drop it in Drive.

Vanessa
Pricing & GTM Operations

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tim Lee <tim.lee@brightcart.com>, procurement@brightcart.com
Date: Tue, 18 Jun 2028 10:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Question on April invoice rounding and context allocation

Vanessa / Jordan / Tim —

Attached is the line-level re-calculation for April using the parameters you asked for: 50% overlap threshold, fractional apportionment across the committed 500k tokens, and a reduced quantum of 256 tokens for long-context bucketization (per the pilot adjustment). Summary:
- Original billed tokens (as invoiced): 612,874
- Recalculated billed tokens (proposed): 562,341
- Difference: 50,533 tokens (~8.25% lower)
- Dollar impact at contracted price (post 10% discount): ~$4,620 credit to BrightCart

I've also included an example calculation (see bottom of sheet) for two representative API calls where the original rounding doubled the billed quantum; the fractional apportionment fixes that.

Next steps: if Tim signs off we'll process a $4,620 credit and flip BrightCart to fractional-apportionment for invoices going forward, plus reduce their long-context quantum to 256 (pilot). I'll also note this in the billing-run SOP.

Attachment: april-recalc-BrightCart.csv

From: Tim Lee <tim.lee@brightcart.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@brightcart.com, Maria Gonzalez <maria.g@brightcart.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Jun 2028 16:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Question on April invoice rounding and context allocation

Jordan / Vanessa / Kimberly —

Thanks for the very clear breakdown and quick re-calc. We agree with the proposed correction and the $4,620 credit sounds right based on our internal checking. We also welcome flipping BrightCart to the fractional-apportionment toggle and trying the 256 quantum for long-context calls — that'll help us forecast.

Just to be explicit on timing: can Redwood post the credit on the July invoice and confirm the toggle change takes effect July 1st? Also please send a short note I can share with FP&A outlining the calculation approach (1 paragraph + table is fine).

If you confirm timing, procurement will close the billing ticket on our side.

Best,
Tim
VP Product, BrightCart
